question.text: For a certain thermochemical reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ΔH</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>77</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>ΔS</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>122</mn><msup><mi>JK</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>log</mi></math> equilibrium constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>logK</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo></math> _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
Given,

 T=400 K,ΔHo=77.2 kJ mol-1,ΔSo=122JK-1

ΔGo=ΔHo-TΔSo

=77.2×103-400×122=28400 J

ΔG°=-2.303 R T log K

Where K is the equilibrium constant.

By putting the values in above equation,

⇒28400=-2.303×8.314×400×log K

⇒log K=-3.708=-37.08×10-1
